articles.title: Game of Thrones Stage Play The Mad King Is Coming to London in 2027
articles.summary: Following a sold-out run at the Royal Shakespeare Company, George R.R. Martin’s Game of Thrones: The Mad King stage play will move to London in 2027.
articles.body:
Game of Thrones: The Mad King is coming to London next year.

Author George R.R. Martin has revealed that the Royal Shakespeare Company will bring the prequel stage play to the UK capital in 2027. A venue or premiere date has not been announced yet.

“I had a splendid time in Stratford upon Avon for the premier of Duncan Macmillan and Dominic Cooke’s epic new stage production of Game of Thrones: The Mad King. And furthermore I’m thrilled to announce that the production will be moving on to London to share the experience with a wider audience,” Martin wrote on his blog .

Game of Thrones: The Mad King began its six-week run in July at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford. It closes this week, having earned rave reviews and many sold out shows.

The play is set roughly 15 years before Martin’s first A Song of Ice and Fire book begins. It chronicles the downfall of King Aerys II Targaryen, aka “The Mad King” who was overthrown during Robert’s Rebellion.

IGN writer Helen O’Hara caught one of the productions during its run at Stratford and broke down 9 things the play reveals about Westeros that Game of Thrones fans would want to know , including how Rhaegar Targaryen was deeply wronged by history and that Daenerys and Jon Snow were conceived on the same night.

articles.title: Hideki Kamiya Tells Xbox CEO He's Ready to Make Scalebound When She Is
articles.summary: Bayonetta creator Hideki Kamiya has a message for Xbox CEO Asha Sharma: When she's ready to make Scalebound, he'll be waiting.
articles.body:
Bayonetta creator Hideki Kamiya has a message for Xbox CEO Asha Sharma: When she's ready to make Scalebound , he'll be waiting.

The action-game mastermind and Clovers studio head spoke about his desire to return to his canceled dragon IP during a recent interview with VGC . It's been a little more than nine years since Microsoft finally, officially confirmed it had shut down Scalebound after PlatinumGames announced it in 2014. Still, Kamiya said he's always ready to breathe life back into it.

When asked if he's contacted Sharma about Scalebound, he said, "Well, no, but now’s my opportunity to once again say that if they want to do it, let’s make it happen!"

"[Clovers president Kento Koyama] is on board too," he added. Kamiya then asked the site to include some of what little Scalebound footage was released to the public just so Sharma could take a look.

Kamiya and the rest of PlatinumGames announced the now-canned Xbox One-exclusive action-RPG 12 years ago at E3 2014. A lot has changed since then.

Scalebound eventually returned for gamescom 2015 , one year later, but then mostly went quiet. A delay to 2017 then stoked fears that the project may be in trouble, with a follow-up report then suggesting it could be in trouble before Microsoft delivered the final blow.

Although Kamiya no longer works at PlatinumGames, he confirmed he had moved on to help form Clovers in late 2024 . Although that team is heads down working on Okami 2 , it doesn't mean he isn't hoping to return to Scalebound one day. It's a project he and other PlatinumGames devs have expressed interest in returning to plenty of times over the years. Now, he's hoping Sharma can help make it happen.

Scalebound Official Screenshots from E3 2016

During his interview with VGC, Kamiya recalled a recent dinner he had with some of the Scalebound team. He noted the canceled video game wasn't the only thing they talked about, but "it did come up a few times," and they "all remembered how fun it was to work" on it.

"Obviously, there were some tough times as well, but the fact that people still look back on that time with a lot of fun is something that I find very gratifying as the director of the project," Kamiya explained. "Of course, it’s very unfortunate that the project was unable to see the light of day ultimately, and that is something that even now I still very strongly desire to be able to see through if it’s all possible, and I’m being one hundred percent serious when I say that.

Kamiya said Clovers "might not be in a position" to work on Scalebound "right this second," but it's still something he's seeking out. He went as far as to say, "I strongly believe that if you want something strongly enough, you eventually find a way to make it happen."

"That’s the case with Okami right now," he continued, "where even after all these years, the opportunity once again presented itself, and I hope that will be the case with Scalebound in the future as well."

Like Kamiya, Xbox has gone through its own changes recently. Sharma took over for Phil Spencer as CEO in February of this year, leading to a waterfall of snappy changes at Microsoft's gaming wing that have been received both positively and negatively by fans. For example, the company announced last week it would allow players to digitize their physical games . That move in particular seems to have gone over well with fans, but it's done little to cushion the blow that came after Xbox announced it would be laying off 3,200 staff and shedding studios like Double Fine and Ninja Theory in July.

Whether Sharma and the rest of Xbox have room to make Scalebound happen remains to be seen. While we wait to see what the future holds, you can read what Kamiya had to say about the game in 2021 .

articles.title: Criminal Showrunner and Winter Soldier Co-Creator Ed Brubaker Sued by Production Assistant
articles.summary: Prime Video's Criminal series is embroiled in controversy, as showrunner Ed Brubaker has been sued by a former production assistant for allegedly fostering a hostile work environment.
articles.body:
Ed Brubaker, co-creator of the Winter Soldier and the indie comics series Criminal, is being sued by a former production assistant on the Criminal TV series. Both Amazon MGM Studios and production company Big Indie Pictures are also named in the suit, which alleges that Brubaker fostered a hostile work environment that included both racial and sexual harassment.

Deadline obtained a copy of the complaint, which was filed by former PA ljaaz Noobu in the Los Angeles Superior Court. The suit consists of no fewer than 12 claims, ranging from sexual and racial harassment to assault and battery.

“This action arises from the sustained sexual, racial, national origin, and religious harassment that Plaintiff ljaaz Noobu, a Sri Lankan American filmmaker with 14 years of experience in the film industry, endured while working on the production of the forthcoming television series Criminal," the complaint reads. "Hired in February 2023 as a production assistant to showrunner and Executive Producer Ed Brubaker, Plaintiff came to the production eager to contribute his talent and technical knowledge to a marquee project. Instead, he was subjected to a workplace made toxic and abusive by the very individuals entrusted with authority over it."

The complaint goes on to list specific allegations of racial and sexual harassment, as well as accusing Brubaker of holding a functional firearm to Noobu's head and pulling the trigger. The complaint also alleges that Noobu was retaliated against and fired from production after requesting a promotion and denied credit for working on the series.

Representatives for Amazon MGM Studios and Brubaker have yet to comment on the lawsuit.

Criminal is based on the long-running Image Comics series created by Brubaker and artist Sean Phillips. Prime Video officially ordered the series in January 2024, with a cast that includes Richard Jenkins, Adria Arjona, Kadeem Hardison, and Charlie Hunnam. Filming on the series took place later that year.

Brubaker is a prolific writer whose comic book career dates back to the early '90s. He's perhaps best known for co-creating the Winter Soldier incarnation of Bucky Barnes as part of his lengthy Captain America run. In recent years, Brubaker has made the transition to Hollywood, writing for series like Westworld and Batman: Caped Crusader before becoming showrunner on Criminal.

articles.title: DLSS 5 Will Be Coming to Older Graphics Cards After All
articles.summary: On Nvidia's forums, an Nvidia employee claimed that the company will be expanding DLSS 5 support to RTX 40 series graphics cards at some point, but we're probably going to be waiting a while for it.
articles.body:
Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering tech officially debuted yesterday in NBA 2K27, and it's only supported on current-generation RTX 5000 graphics cards. But it seems like that'll change over time.

On Nvidia's forums, an employee claimed that the company will be expanding DLSS 5 support to RTX 40 series graphics cards at some point, but we're probably going to wait a while for it. He said, "Our current focus is on optimizing performance for the GeForce RTX 50 Series with model updates expected later this fall," but noted that "once RTX 50 Series performance is more fully tuned, we plan to work on expanding official support to the GeForce RTX 40 Series."

So, it seems like the company's focus, at least for now, is to get it running smoother on current-generation graphics cards before retrofitting it to its Ada Lovelace architecture. That makes a lot of sense, too. I've briefly messed around with the technology in NBA 2K27, and I was surprised by how subtle the changes were, at least compared to some of the nightmare fuel I've seen on Reddit. But even though the technology did make NBA 2K27 look better, it had a massive impact to performance, and I was testing it on an RTX 5090 .

Turning on DLSS 5 on my main system brought the pre-frame-gen frame rate down from around 57-60 fps down to around 37 fps, a pretty massive 43% performance drop. If that's the performance hit on the most powerful graphics card on the market, I'm not confident about how well something like the RTX 4080 would handle it, especially with its older Tensor Cores.

It's clear that Nvidia has made a lot of headway in optimizing the technology since it was first revealed back in March, though. Back then, Nvidia needed two RTX 5090s to even run it, and now Team Green claims that it has improved model performance by around 5x. There's a possibility that with enough optimization, the performance hit will shrink over time. But, until I actually see that, I'm going to remain skeptical.

articles.title: New Resident Evil Teaser Trailer Reveals First Glimpse at Creature That Looks a Lot Like Las Plagas
articles.summary: A new Spanish-language trailer for Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie includes never-before-seen footage of a tentacle-like mutation that looks frighteningly similar to Las Plagas from RE4.
articles.body:
A new Spanish-language teaser trailer for Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie includes never-before-seen footage of a tentacle-like mutation that looks frighteningly similar to Las Plagas from Resident Evil 4.

The teaser, published on September 4, 2026, sees Bryan Hodukavich (played by Austin Abrams) cautiously walk into the maternity ward of a hospital, which seems to have been overtaken by some kind of fleshy substance — and, tragically, so have all the bassinets meant to hold newborn babies.

Another shot from the trailer shows a corpse’s feet being consumed by thin, wormlike vines. That corpse raises itself up a second later, seemingly animated by one of these vines protruding from its cheek as a horrified Hodukavich looks on.

Zach Cregger’s RESIDENT EVIL new international teaser featuring exclusive footage has just been released. It’s tracking to be this fall’s highest-grossing film, recording a $60M-$80M domestic debut. pic.twitter.com/Jtjr0FqRLN — Global Box Office (@GlobalBoxOffice) September 4, 2026

Zach Cregger’s RESIDENT EVIL new international teaser featuring exclusive footage has just been released. It’s tracking to be this fall’s highest-grossing film, recording a $60M-$80M domestic debut. pic.twitter.com/Jtjr0FqRLN

Needless to say, this has already sparked comparisons to Las Plagas, the parasite responsible for the Los Illuminados Incident in RE4. That particular mutation notably boasted tentacle-like growths, which would transform into terrifying beings as their growth stages progressed.

Cregger has been open about his inspiration for his Resident Evil movie, saying that RE4 and RE7 had the biggest influence on his creative approach to the film. "I like the idea of borrowing the rhythm and scale from [Resident Evil] 4 and using some of the character elements from [Resident Evil] 7," he said in a September 1 Reddit AMA.

"7 is when Ethan comes into it, and I like that you're just a normal dude going through this horrible situation. 4 has the rhythm that I really like where you're moving from set piece to set piece and location to location. 4 is such a big game. You go through all these different – it feels like worlds, from the village to the castle, to the island. It's just like, it keeps giving and giving."

𝚃𝚑𝚎 𝚜𝚞𝚋𝚓𝚎𝚌𝚝 𝚒𝚜… 𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚒𝚗𝚐. pic.twitter.com/nIesJoLqF7 — Resident Evil (@ResidentEvil) September 4, 2026

𝚃𝚑𝚎 𝚜𝚞𝚋𝚓𝚎𝚌𝚝 𝚒𝚜… 𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚒𝚗𝚐. pic.twitter.com/nIesJoLqF7

That wasn’t the only exciting reveal from Cregger’s Resident Evil movie today; the film’s official social media accounts also shared a promotional poster showing X-ray imaging of a Doberman Pinscher — the dog breed that famously antagonizes players in several of the early games. The post’s caption reads: "The subject is… changing," implying that this particular Doberman has been infected with the T-Virus.

It’s a lovely callback to the earlier Resident Evil games and yet another Easter egg that Cregger has included in his interpretation of the series, alongside a wealth of other references that connect his vision to the source material.

Cregger’s movie tells a new story that follows an average Joe who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. Although he was staunchly against making a one-to-one recreation of the games to avoid rehashing "stories that [they] tell so well," Cregger understands why fans might be hesitant to give him a chance, telling IGN in an interview that he was "naive" to think fans would be onboard with him avoiding a direct adaptation of the games.

articles.title: GTA 6 for Xbox: You Can Save $10, Today Only

articles.body:
Here’s a good deal for any Xbox Series X|S owner who hasn’t preordered Grand Theft Auto 6 yet. Today only, by taking advantage of an Xbox gift card deal at Newegg , you can effectively knock $10 off the price of GTA 6.

How does it work, you ask? Newegg is offering $5 off $50 Xbox gift cards if you enter promo code LDSF373 at checkout . Thankfully, the code stacks, so you can add two gift cards to your cart to get $10 off $100 worth of credit.

As luck would have it, the ultimate edition of GTA 6, the one most people are buying , is available to preorder on Xbox for $99.99 . Put it all together, and you effectively save $10 off GTA 6. But remember, the deal is good today only.

Grand Theft Auto VI - Ultimate Edition (Xbox)

Why preorder GTA 6 at all? It can be safely assumed that the game will carry a massive file size. If you preorder, you can preload it starting November 12 , a week ahead of launch. That way it’ll be installed on your system and ready to play the moment it comes out.

We had only gotten a sprinkling of specifics about GTA 6 over the past few years until last week’s extended look blew the game open with 27 minutes of frankly awesome-looking gameplay footage. I was expecting it to look incredible, but it actually exceeded my expectations. Games like this don’t come around often.

IGN’s own Rachel Weber got to see a lot more than those 27 minutes of the game, and also got to chat with the co-studio head Rob Nelson about it. Check out her preview for a ton of new GTA 6 info.

Personally, I’ve been debating which console to play GTA 6 on , and I’m leaning toward Xbox, so I think I’m going to take advantage of this gift card deal. I like the Xbox controller better (though the Wolverine PS5 controller looks pretty stellar), and I’m also a big fan of the Quick Resume function. But really, I imagine it’ll play just fine on both consoles.

I posted a similar deal for PS5 yesterday, but that one has ended, just as this one will end at midnight tonight. However, even if you missed out, all hope is not lost. GTA 6 doesn’t come out until November 19, and Newegg offers discounts on PlayStation and Xbox gift cards fairly often. I’d say it’s likely this deal will come back around before the big launch.

articles.title: Flexispot's Labor Day Sale Takes Up to 65% Off Office Furniture, Including Our Favorite Standing Desk of 2026
articles.summary: Flexispot is best known for its standing desks and ergo chairs, but the brand has since expanded to home furniture.
articles.body:
Labor Day regularly plays host to some of the best deals on home office furniture, especially since the back to school hubbub is coming to a close and a lot of merchants are trying to move the last of their inventory. If you're in the market for an electric standing desk or an ergonomic chair, then Flexispot is kicking off a Labor Day Sale that you'll want to check out.

Flexispot is best known for its line of affordable yet premium standing desks, and fortunately their best selling models are all discounted. The brand has since branched out to produce other types of home furniture that includes Japanese joinery bed frames, memory foam mattresses, power lift chairs, and electric sleeper sofas. These are, in a nutshell, well-made replicas of far pricier products, and if you prioritize value over brand loyalty, then you're bound to save a lot of money.

In addition to the itemized discounts, Flexispot is also offering a 10% off coupon code " FSIGNOFF " that works on all products sidewide and stacks with existing discounts. This coupon expires September 30.

Save Up to 65% Off During the Flexispot Labor Day Sale

Flexispot E7L L-Shaped Electric Standing Desk

Flexispot C7 Ergonomic Chair (New Model)

Flexispot Lotus Smart Electric Recliner and Rocker

You can quickly browse through all of the listed products on sale above. For more information on each product and why they are worth your consideration, read through below.

Flexispot E7 Pro Desk starting at $359.99

Flexispot has established a reputation for producing quality electric standing desks with premium features at a fraction of the price compared to other reputable brands. We like Flexispot because it offers quality electric standing desks with all the features you'd want at a fraction of the price compared to other more well-known models. We rated Flexispot's highest- end model, the E7 Pro, the best overall standing desk of 2025 .

The E7 Pro is the creme de la creme of Flexispot's standing desks. It's recent released so it isn't nearly as heavily discounted as the other models. Currently it costs $359.99 (normally $599.99) after coupon for the base only and desktop surfaces start at $80. The E7 Pro features the best build quality of the three listed here, and it certainly shows with a weight capacity of a whopping 440lbs. Flexispot claims the motor for the E7 Pro is superior to the standard dual motor setup you'll find in the E5 and E7 and other brands, offering smoother and faster movement. You also get more cable management options included than even the E7. The Flexispot E7 Pro comes with an extended 15-year warranty on all metal, mechanical, and electrical parts and components, including the motor.

The Flexispot E5 desk is, in my opinion, the best value electric standing desk while still offering all the premium features you'd want. Right now it costs $206.99 (normally $379.99) after coupon for the base only and desktop surfaces start at $80. The Flexispot E5 is the least expensive model featuring dual motors , which are preferred over a single motor because they can support more weight (in this case 287lbs max) and they last longer because the stress is evenly distributed. The desktop is supported by a double crossbeam structure so that your surface is evenly supported to prevent any sagging. Most standing desks in this price range only have legs with a two-stage column, but this one features a three-stage column, which supports a greater vertical range (in this case 23.6" to 49.2"). An anti-collision feature, a must-have in all desks, will stop the desk when it detects obstruction of the motor. Finally, the keypad controls offer three memory presets and a timer to remind you when to swap sit/stand positions. The E5 comes with a 10-year warranty.

The E7 currently costs $269.99 (normally $499.99) after coupon for the base only and desktop surfaces start at $80. For an extra $140, the Flexispot E7 offers better build quality, a higher weight threshold, more included accessories, and a longer warranty. The lifting capacity has been upgraded from 287lbs to 355lbs. Aesthetically, the legs look more professional, with laser-welded seams, powder-coated finish, and no visible holes. The advanced keyboard has been upgraded with an LCD display, more memory presets, a built-in USB charger, and a child-lock function that's a necessity for those of us with inquisitive toddlers. The E7 also comes with a built-in cable tray under the desk to stow away all of your messy wiring. The Flexispot E7 comes with a 15 year warranty like the E7 Pro.

Flexispot E7L L-Shaped Desk starting at $476.99

An L-shaped desk is the best way to take advantage of room corners that are otherwise hard to utilize efficiently. Fortunately, Flexispot makes an L-shaped variant of its E7 desk, with the frame starting at $476.99. You'll only need to add $80 to get a 63"x47"x24" chipboard desktop surface included. The desk boasts a triple motor system (one for each leg) with a maximum weight capacity is 330 pounds and a height range of 25" to 50.7". The keyboard features a digital display, four memory presets, a built-in USB charger, and a child-lock function. Like the E7, the E7L includes a 15 year warranty.

Flexispot C7 Ergonomic Chair for $269.99

The Flexispot C7 offers a ton of features that are typically reserved for much more expensive chairs. This includes an automatically adjusting lumbar system, adjustable seat depth, adjustable armrests, adjustable seat tilt, adjustable headrest, 128 degrees of recline, and more. There's also a C7 Max Ergonomic Chair available starting at $387 which features a thicker seat cushion, greater recline adjustability, and 5D armrests, and the option to add a built-in footrest.

Flexispot Japanese Joinery Bed Frame starting at $314.99

You've probably heard of Thuma , a pricey manufacturer of bed frames that use traditional Japanese joinery instead of screws. Flexispot has a very similar product that employs the same joinery techniques, is made of the same solid rubberwood material, and nearly the same weight capacity (1,200lbs vs 1,500 lbs), but costs only a third of the price. The Flexispot Kana Bed Frame starts at $349.99 for the full size with queen and king sizes also available. You can opt to add in a solid rubberwood headboard for an additional $270 or a washable linen pillowboard for $280.

Flexispot Premier Hybrid Mattress starting at $332.99

Continuing down the bedroom lineup, Flexispot also carries a "premier hybrid mattress" that borrows its name from the more well known Nectar Premier Hybrid Mattress . However, while Nectar's queen-sized mattress starts at $1,100, Flexispot sells its version for only $449.99. The construction is remarkably similar as well, which includes 5 total inches of foam (2" of gel foam, 2" of gel memory foam, and 1" PU foam), as well as 8 inches of individually wrapped pocket coils.

Flexispot Lotus Electric Rocker Recliner starting at $377.99

Flexispot now sells sectionals, sofas, and recliners at affordable prices. The Lotus Smart Rocker is a pretty sweet addition to your gaming den, especially if you opt for the electric version starting at $377.99. It's available in both fabric and PU leather upholstery and features full electric reclinability. It can also swivel up to 270 degrees and has a smooth rocking function. There are USB ports for charging your phone, tablet, or gaming handheld, and even a handy storage cubby.

Consider getting a desk frame here and the desktop surface elsewhere

I have three standing desks. One of the standing desks included a desktop, however for the other two desks I sourced on my own. For one of them I purchased a massive 74"x26" maple veneered countertop from Ikea for $199. For the other one I purchased a 48"x25" solid wood countertop from Home Depot and finished it myself. There are more options available where you could save money, opt for a better quality material, or both. Just remember to abide by the weight limitations.

How does Flexispot compare to other brands?

I can only speak from personal experience. I own a Jarvis Fully, a Vari Ergo, and a Flexispot E5. All three are excellent desks that have caused me no problems whatsoever in the 3+ years of owning them, and that's the point. The Flexispot E5 is considerably less expensive than the other two options, and yet I don't really see where much of that cost is going. For a similar price of a barebones $600 Jarvis standing desk (which is now owned by MillerKnoll), you could get the top end Flexispot E7 Pro and still come out with a few hundred dollars left over.

articles.title: Hands-On With Acer's Prototype Convertible Handheld PC/Laptop Hybrid
articles.summary: It works like a gaming handheld when you want to play, and then you can open it up into a mini, almost Netbook-like PC in just a few short seconds.
articles.body:
Europe's biggest tech show, IFA, is currently underway in Berlin, Germany, and Acer decided to show off not one, but two working prototypes of its "Project DualPlay Mini."

The handheld gaming PC seems fairly innocuous at first glance, other than its aggressive, brand-appropriate Predator styling, but a quick lift of its front gaming panel and a subtle flip of its screen turns it into a surprisingly adequate mini PC.

It's very important, now that I've hyped this up, for me to mention this is only a prototype. This isn't something you can buy anytime soon, if ever. Acer told me they're basically feeling out the market with it, seeing if there's enough interest. Now this is purely anecdotal, but an informal survey of "me" says "yes, please, I want this device in my life."

For a prototype with no solid release plan, the Project DualPlay Mini was surprisingly full-featured. I played Forza Horizon 6 and it looked great, and I was really surprised there were rumble features built in. If there was anything pre-release about the rumble feature, it's that it was surprisingly loud. But other than that, it worked really well and helped add an extra dimension to the already cool experience.

The buttons and joysticks also felt awesome, with great tactile feedback and an extremely smooth thumbstick experience. The screen looked amazing, although Acer's representative wouldn't give me much in the way of specs since the units on display are still in the prototype phase.

Turning from gaming to mini laptop mode is legitimately fun. You just open up the top and give the screen a little flip to get it into laptop mode. The one big downer here is there's no trackpad, but the prototype did have a touch screen, and I had no trouble navigating around the Windows 11 desktop and in the Steam app.

Honestly, when I first opened it up into laptop mode, I got heavy 2011-esque Netbook vibes, and I say that from a place of love. Those teeny Netbooks are just old enough now to evoke some wistful nostalgia for that weird age when smart phones weren't quite smart enough but regular laptops were still too clunky. I found the keyboard to be a pleasure, as far as laptop keyboards go, and while it's meant to be a convertible gaming handheld, the WASD and arrow keys are highlighted on the face of the keys.

This could be the best way to play mouse and keyboard on a handheld device, should it ever become a reality. And honestly, after my very brief time with it, I want so badly for it to be real. It's the best of both worlds and I feel like busting one of these out on the train or the airplane would have the same feel as busting out a T-Mobile Sidekick circa 2006.

articles.title: Bungie Confirms Plans to Sublease Parts of Its Enormous Bellevue Headquarters Following Mass Layoffs
articles.summary: Bungie has responded after announcing plans to sublease 210,984-square feet of its massive headquarters in Bellevue, Washington, saying this move reflects its continued focus on a “digital first” model.
articles.body:
Bungie has confirmed it is "exploring options" to sublease 210,984 square feet of its massive headquarters in Bellevue, Washington, saying the move reflects its continued focus on a "digital first" model.

Following major layoffs across Bungie’s team in June, the studio has made the decision to put a large chunk of its Bellevue headquarters up for sublease, meaning that it’ll be renting out parts of the space to a third party (or parties).

The Game Post broke the news after reportedly reviewing a 10-page advertisement for the building in a commercial leasing brochure, which stated that 210,984 square feet of the building will be available to sublease through September 30, 2035. That’s a long time from now, and one that left fans concerned for Bungie's future projects.

Bungie confirmed the news in a statement sent to The Game Post, stating that this move reflects the company’s growing focus on remote work, which ties into its "digital-first" model.

"Bungie is exploring options to sublease its campus in Bellevue, Washington," a studio spokesperson said. "The studio transitioned to a digital-first model several years ago, and this move reflects the team’s evolving workplace needs and the effectiveness of its remote collaboration. Bungie will continue to maintain a physical office presence in Bellevue."

Responses from the community have been mixed; some argue that this change is only logical, given the massive layoffs that just occurred, while others are about what this could mean for Bungie’s future.

"I’ve seen people dooming about this like it doesn’t make a ton of sense in the present circumstances," one wrote on X. "400-something people aren’t gonna be able to use that space in full, and it’s better than letting it collect dust."

"Bungie is so good at making games (imo) that I wish they could fill all this space and have 2-5 projects at once,” another said . “But with their reduced size now, it’s probably the wise decision."

"In layman's terms, 'We're all going to be working from home now, since we can no longer afford our massive offices,'" another remarked.

Bungie notably laid off 292 workers at its Bellevue, Washington office in June, marking its third round of layoffs in three years. As per reporting from The Seattle Times , this location employed 1,000 staff members in 2023; the company reportedly laid off approximately 320 employees between October 2023 and July 2024, making this most recent round of layoffs even more brutal.

This latest news follows growing discontent from Bungie’s fanbase, who recently took to the chat en masse during PlayStation’s September State of Play to spam requests for Destiny 3 after the developer ended support for the title in favor of focusing on Marathon earlier this year.

Sources told Forbes that plans were in place to 'relaunch' the game as Destiny Infinity, but they were ultimately scrapped. Destiny 3 was also reportedly considered by Bungie, but "things didn't swing that way."

articles.title: Rockstar Censors GTA 6 Extended Look Trailer for China
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has published a heavily censored version of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look reveal for China.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has published a heavily censored version of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look reveal for China.

As shared by @videotech on X/Twitter , the studio behind the game that is convincing publishers to steer clear of November published its 27-minute gameplay reveal on Chinese social media platform Bilibili last week – but some things are just a bit different from other uploads (via Kotaku ). It doesn't take long to realize that large portions of the GTA 6 trailer have been blurred out, including dancing, drug-related content, and sexual content.

Considering this is a Grand Theft Auto game, there's quite a bit you can't see. Footage of protagonists Jason and Lucia at a nightclub, for example, basically turns the screen into a giant purple blur. A later scene blurs out Jason's hand when he's smoking, while brief shots of the beach censor some of the crowd. While most corpses seem unblurred, footage showing close-ups of bloodied dead bodies has also been completely censored.

GTA 6 Extended Look Censored Video - Screenshots

It's a very different look at GTA 6, but the video wasn't originally the blurry mess we see here. As spotted by GTAForums user BDF , this reportedly isn't the same video Rockstar originally uploaded following GTA 6: Extended Look's Netflix premiere.

The first upload supposedly didn't have the same censoring it does now. Rockstar is said to have altered the video around August 31. The reasoning behind the delayed adjustments is unclear.

BDF noted that the changes have split users on China's Reddit-like platform, Tieba, and other online communities. While some suspect Rockstar censored GTA 6 to keep younger users from viewing the trailer's contents, others believe the move reflects prejudice from Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive. BDF also reported that Rockstar and Take-Two have issued DMCA takedowns for those reposting unblurred content on Bilibili.

Censored or not, the floodgates for GTA 6 seem to officially be open ahead of its November 19 launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X | S. New Vice City-themed PS5 controllers were revealed just yesterday, additional screenshots were posted on Rockstar's website earlier this week, and fans are still combing through every detail from last week's big gameplay reveal .

There will surely be plenty more to show before that release date finally rolls around. Until then, you can see IGN's coverage, including our preview and interview with the team at Rockstar.

articles.title: How to Watch Free Movies and TV Shows on Your PS5
articles.body:
Sony recently announced an entirely new feature for PS5 users: free live TV. In short, any PS5 owner with a PlayStation account now has access to a range of ad-supported live TV channels directly through their console, no extra charge.

Still, the new “Live TV on PS5” feature isn’t the only way you can watch movies and TV for free. Below, I’ve broken down how to access the new app, as well as what other (potentially better) free media options you have on your console.

How to Watch Live TV for Free on Your PS5

To access the new live TV channels, you’ll need a PlayStation 5 and a PlayStation account. Right now, the new Live TV feature is only available in the U.S., with plans to expand into Canada in the near future.

While PlayStation technically says the service doesn't require a subscription, this PlayStation account will be used to link to a Sony Core Pictures account, which predates this new feature. It’s what you’d use to buy or rent movies and series through your PlayStation, kind of similar to Prime Video , and is also available as a separate streaming subscription .

The user interface replicates the cable style of live TV, giving you an opportunity to see upcoming schedules for each available channel. As with most modern streaming interfaces, you’ll also get personalized and themed recommendations.

You won’t have endless access to the live TV channels you’d get out of a paid subscription like Hulu + Live TV or ESPN Unlimited . Instead, the offerings are more like reruns from classic channels. You get free movies from channels like MovieSphere and Sony One Horror Hits, and channels dedicated to full TV shows like Community, The Walking Dead, and Naruto . You’ll also get limited sport programming as well as local news and weather through NBC and Fox.

In truth, the selection isn't likely vary too much from other free ad-supported television (FAST, as some like to call it) channels. Speaking of…

This new feature isn’t technically your own free live TV option. There’s two other particularly great free streaming apps you can access on PS5 consoles, though you’ll have to download them as individual apps as opposed to accessing them directly from the Media menu.

Pluto TV is under the Paramount umbrella and offers its own spread of over 400 channels, including tons of free movies and shows. That Paramount umbrella gets you a pretty wild range, including the John Wick movies, Top Gun: Maverick, Pitch Perfect, and ridiculous amounts of Star Trek . You’ll also get access to some local CBS news stations.

Tubi was acquired by Fox back in 2020, and its been on a bit of a tear since then. Its picked up some classic cartoons that were previously dropped by streamers like HBO Max , and also happens to have a great selection of anime . You never know what you’ll find on Tubi, but some big hits include the Kung Fu Panda movies, Men in Black, and the Jurassic World movies . Tubi also offers live TV, including sports reruns and local news under that Fox banner.

Yeah, it’s not exactly free TV shows or movies, but if you’re looking for solid and free entertainment, you’ll definitely find something on the classics: YouTube and Twitch. These are both also available as apps through your PS5, and as long as you’re cool with some ads, have probably more hours of content than anything else.

Despite Sony’s double State of Play this week being a little bit of a dud — though did you catch the hard-as-hell new Resident Evil clip at the very beginning? — the trailer-sphere nonetheless kept chugging along as it always does. We got a new look at Street Fighter and a bunch more trailers ahead of Venice and Toronto Film Festivals for movies that are already catching Oscar buzz, a holdover from gamescom, and an indie game that caught my attention at the Tribeca Festival this past summer. These are the trailers worth checking out this week (and here’s what you missed last week ).

It’s been about four months since the last Street Fighter trailer, and with a little more than a month before release, I’m excited we got another 3-ish minute taste of what to expect from the Kitao Sakurai-directed movie. I might never not be taken aback by blond Noah Centineo as Ken, but the tone of this movie remains convincingly super fun. Like Eric Andre spittles in the new trailer, “This is STREET FIGHTERRRRR!”

Street Fighter releases in theaters October 16.

As we’ve already previewed out of SGF , the combat definitely looks more difficult than RGG’s other non-turn-based games, but I’m glad they still found a way to make early-to-mid-1900s street goons look nearly as ridiculous as present-day Kamurocho.

articles.title: Hideki Kamiya Isn't Fussed About the Physical vs. Digital Debate – He Just Wants Games to Be Preserved for Future Generations
articles.summary: Hideki Kamiya, creator of Bayonetta and director of Resident Evil 2, says he isn’t too fussed about physical vs digital games; instead, he’s more concerned with preserving games for players to enjoy in the future.
articles.body:
Hideki Kamiya, creator of Bayonetta and director of Resident Evil 2, said he isn’t too fussed about physical vs digital games; instead, he’s more concerned with preserving games for players to enjoy in the future.

Hideki Kamiya is behind some of the biggest franchises in gaming history. From Bayonetta to Devil May Cry, Resident Evil 2, and Okami, he’s a veteran of the industry. As such, fans are naturally curious about his stance on the current debate surrounding PlayStation’s plans to end production of all physical game discs starting January 2028.

In his usual candid manner, Kamiya admitted he doesn’t actually buy physical games at all anymore, as told in a September 2 interview with Video Games Chronicle.

"I don’t buy a single physical game these days – every single game I buy is 100% digital, so I look at that decision and think, 'Yeah, I guess this is where things were heading,'" he told the outlet.

He went on to say that the disc vs digital debate isn’t really relevant for him; instead, he hopes publishers make efforts to preserve their games for future generations of players, no matter what form that might take.

"That’s the big thing for me, is whether or not the IP holders are going to take responsibility for ensuring that all of these games will continue to be available to future generations in order for them to be played. Whether that’s physically or digitally is less important to me, just so long as these games will be available to people in the future," he continued.

"Because, as you know, there are already so many of these older classic games that are not playable on modern hardware at all, and I hope that the IP holders will recognize that and continue to make those games available to future people not just from a gameplay perspective, but also from a game culture perspective, and to continue to foster and grow that that culture of gaming. So to me, it’s less important whether the games are made available physically or digitally, but that they’re made available at all."

Kamiya’s thinking reflects a trend in the gaming industry that's cropped up over the last decade; many publishers have begun re-releasing their older games for modern platforms, with some remaking them completely. While it’s a good way to profit from studios' previous work, it also allows these games to be experienced by a new generation of players on updated hardware, or re-experienced by longtime fans without them having to dig out their AV cables.

Other fan-driven initiatives, such as the Stop Killing Games movement and the Video Game History Foundation, aim to protect games both for posterity and consumer rights. Stop Killing Games, which recently joined a Dutch consumer group in a lawsuit against PlayStation, hopes to install legal framework to require publishers to maintain servers for live-service games after official support has ended, while the Video Game History Foundation collects games to "preserve, celebrate, and teach" the public about the history of video games.

There's still a strong movement from players rallying against PlayStation's version for an all-digital future, though. Lawmakers in Mexico have even introduced an anti-trust lawsuit against the company over its decision to end physical discs, accusing it of engaging in “anti-competitive practices."

articles.title: Tetris Responds After Trump Administration Launches 'Build the Wall' Clone Game
articles.summary: Official Tetris pages have responded after the Trump administration launched a clone video game called 'Build the Wall.'
articles.body:
Official Tetris pages have responded after the Trump administration launched a clone video game called 'Build the Wall.'

The Tetris Company joined the backlash after Donald Trump's White House published its Arcade.Gov website today. Amongst a line of games on offer, which includes a Flappy Bird clone called 'Flappy Bill' and a Snake clone called 'Rio Run,' is Build the Wall.

A description for the game follows: "Protect the border from the coming horde." It's a message that Tetris wants absolutely nothing to do with.

"At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it said. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."

Tetris continued, confirming that it had nothing to do with the Trump administration's Build the Wall game. It also added, "We take copyright infringement very seriously." The Tetris Company does not seem to have taken any sort of legal action against the arcade page yet.

The White House launched its website yesterday. It contains five games, including titles asking players to "border patrol along the Rio Grande" and "fill your kids' Trump accounts." It also warned that more games are coming soon.

Arcade.Gov immediately faced backlash from users online. Many have called on companies pulled from the site's reveal video, including Tetris and Sega, to take action. Although the latter has yet to chime in, Tetris is being quite vocal – and so are its fans. Some of its statement's top comments note that games such as this are typically about breaking walls, not building them. Others are just happy to see Tetris speaking up.

CAN'T STOP WINNING. 🎮 Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account. LIVE - PLAY NOW 📲 pic.twitter.com/2nr2jG1ZRg

The Tetris Company's Kerri Brusca also provided The Verge with a statement on the matter: "For more than 40 years, Tetris has brought people together across generations and cultures through play and joy. The objective of the game has always been to stack with purpose to clear as many lines as possible. We are currently reviewing the matter."

IGN reported on the site's original launch earlier today. The Trump administration has stirred controversy with similar moves in the past, including posts referencing the Halo series . Although Microsoft was silent on that matter, The Pokémon Company and Master Chief actor Steve Downes are amongst those who have spoken up .

articles.title: Spider-Noir Canceled at Prime Video After One Season
articles.summary: Amazon's Prime Video has canceled Nicolas Cage's Spider-Noir after just one season.
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Video has canceled Nicolas Cage's Spider-Noir after just one season.

It's an early demise for Cage's live-action take on the wall-crawling hero, as reported by Deadline . The decision arrived just four months after all eight episodes of Spider-Noir Season 1 premiered with a binge release in May 2026.

Spider-Noir was the second Marvel series ordered by Prime Video, and although Cage's time as the detective hero has come to an end, Marvel apparently isn't down for the count quite yet. It's reported that more superhero projects could arrive through the streamer as part of a multi-title deal between Amazon MGM and Sony Pictures Television. Both entities are reportedly working on multiple projects, and although one of them is said to be nearing a series order, details have yet to be announced.

If you watched Spider-Noir, there's a good chance you're sad to see it won't come back for Season 2. Critics and fans alike generally adored the crime drama superhero spin, with Rotten Tomatoes recording 92% favorability for the latter and 90% for the former. IGN liked Season 1, too, awarding it an 8/10 review .

"Nicolas Cage’s Bogie-meets-Bugs Bunny pulp hero invigorates the highly entertaining, genre-bending Spider-Noir," we said at the time of its Prime Video premiere.

Spider-Noir follows Cage's Ben Reilly, a private investigator with spider-like powers who helps his friends and clients alike in 1930s New York City. In addition to its web-swinging star, it also featured Lamorne Morris as Robbie Robertson, Li Jun Li as Cat Hardy, and Karen Rodriguez as Janet Ruiz. Other classic Marvel characters, such as Sandman (Jack Huston) and Tombstone (Abraham Popoola), also played a role in the series.

Spider-Noir Black-and-White and Color Images

Fans found more than a mystery plot and characters to love. Spider-Noir also featured a novel concept that saw the show available to watch entirely in black-and-white or in color , giving viewers not only a slightly more personalized experience but even a reason to rewatch scenes, too. Unfortunately, it seems to have done little to convince audiences to give the show the support it needed to carry on.

As reported by Deadline, Nielsen recorded 2.6 billion viewing minutes in the first six weeks following its premiere. It was a strong enough start that petered out after it quickly fell from Prime Video's top 10 charts.

What lies in store for Amazon, Sony, and Prime Video's Marvel plans remains unclear. Another Spider-Man-style project called Silk: Spider Society was once said to be in the works, but was eventually canceled .

articles.title: Zach Cregger Already Has 'Ideas' About What He'd Do for a Second Resident Evil Movie
articles.summary: Zach Cregger says he'd love to tell more stories in the Resident Evil universe, admitting he already has "ideas" about where he’d take things in a second film.
articles.body:
Zach Cregger says he’d love to tell more stories in the Resident Evil universe, admitting he already has "ideas" about where he'd take things in a second film.

Cregger’s Resident Evil movie releases on September 18, 2026. It’s a decidedly different take on Capcom’s flagship horror franchise that tells a totally original tale, following an average Joe who’s forced to navigate the chaos of the Raccoon City Incident.

This decision has, unsurprisingly, split the series' fanbase — but Cregger has maintained that he’s a huge fan of the games and didn’t just "slap" Resident Evil onto the movie to "get a budget." In fact, he’s already got an idea of where he’d take a second film if everything goes well.

When asked if he’d like to remain in the Resident Evil universe during an interview with The Playlist , Cregger answered: "I can’t help thinking about other places this story could go. I’ve got ideas, but this movie hasn’t even come out yet. Let’s see what happens.

"With Barbarian, I’ve never entertained the idea of a sequel or another movie in that universe because that story is, at its heart, so foul," he continued. "What makes Barbarian interesting is the unfolding of the narrative, not the subject matter. I don’t think I want to write another story about what that movie is about. But this is different. I want to talk about the ending of this movie so badly, because there is a big aspect of it that’s worth discussing. This is a different situation."

Thankfully, Resident Evil is already shaping up to have the most successful movie launch in the franchise’s history; early predictions suggest the horror flick could earn $40M – $50M during its opening weekend, potentially outearning any other movie adaptation of the game series.

Excitement (and trepidation) for Cregger’s version of events is at an all-time high, and regular teasers have been rolling out showing more and more of what we can expect when September 18 arrives. Most recently, a Spanish-language trailer from Sony España showed a glimpse of a creature that looks an awful lot like it’s been overtaken by Las Plagas, the parasite Leon fights in Resident Evil 4.

A promotional poster was also shared on the movie’s official social media accounts that showed an X-ray of a Doberman Pinscher, suggesting that the T-Virus infected dogs will make a possible appearance in the movie as a lovely callback to the earlier games.

For now, we’ll just have to wait and see if Resident Evil lives up to the hype — or lack thereof, with Cregger telling us that he was "naive" to expect all fans of the games would be happy with his decision to avoid a direct adaptation of "stories the games tell so well."

articles.title: The Odyssey Surpasses $1 Billion at International Box Office With Weeks Left In Theaters
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has earned more than $1 billion at the international box office, and it still has nearly four more weeks left in theaters.
articles.body:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has earned more than $1 billion at the international box office, and it still has nearly four more weeks left in theaters.

The Odyssey is enjoying a hugely successful theatrical run. Reports from Deadline confirm Nolan’s retelling of the ancient Greek epic has earned $1.59 billion at the global box office, becoming the director’s most profitable film to date and the 17th movie to ever cross the $1B mark internationally. (For reference, the global box office adds all markets together, while the international box office concerns markets outside of North America. You can check out our coverage of the film crossing $1B at the global box office here. )

What’s more, it’s the first standalone, non-sequel and non-remake to do so since James Cameron’s Avatar in 2009; other films that have crossed this line include Avengers: Endgame , Star Wars: The Force Awakens, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day , to name a few.

"From its record-breaking opening to this historic milestone, The Odyssey has captivated audiences around the world," Universal Pictures International’s president of distribution, Veronika Kwan Vandenberg, said in a statement. "We are incredibly proud to have partnered with Christopher Nolan, Emma Thomas and everyone at Syncopy to share this visionary theatrical experience with audiences everywhere."

The Odyssey previously broke another big record in late August, overtaking Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest-grossing R-Rated film of all time. The news earned a humorous congratulations from Ryan Reynolds , who posted a video mashup of Deadpool’s fight against Wolverine in the Honda Odyssey between clips of Odysseus and his men walking through the forest of giants.

"Obviously, [The Odyssey] is an incredible, incredible movie. Christopher Nolan literally breathes the rarest air on Earth. He's a singular filmmaker. I mean, Matt Damon, Tom Holland, who's clearly batting a thousand stars with Zendaya. I just love that people are going to the movie theaters. I don’t even care why or for what reason. Just go to the movie theaters. There’s no better shared experience," the actor told Variety .

There’s still time to see The Odyssey as Nolan intended, with 70mm IMAX showings of the film extended until September 30 due to the small amount of screens that exist in the world. This is the second time these screenings have been extended, likely adding on to its already hugely profitable box office run.

The Odyssey dominated the movies this summer alongside Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which swung past Avengers: Endgame’s record to become the highest-grossing domestic film in history, as well as the most profitable Spider-Man movie of all time, becoming the first one to reach $2 billion in theaters.

If you needed a reason to see the Odyssey before its extended screenings end, check out our review right here on IGN, where we scored Nolan’s version of the epic an 8 out of 10, calling it a "must-watch cinematic experience."

articles.title: The Fury of Dracula Board Game Is a Supernatural Horror Game of Cat and Mouse All the Right Ways
articles.body:
The “hidden movement” genre of board games is one of my favorites and I still remember where I discovered this type of game. I was watching Wil Wheaton’s “Tabletop” series, when the game of the week was “Fury of Dracula”, a game where one person assumes the role of Dracula, spreading terror and attempting to grow his vampire forces around the globe, while the others are vampire hunters, try to track him down and drive a stake through his heart. Despite falling in love with what I saw, it was unfortunately at a time when Fury was out of print, and while eventually I would find myself a copy, it remained a rather sought after game for fellow hidden movement fans. Thankfully, at long last, the good folks at Avalon Hill have brought it back in a brand new 5th Edition, and fans around the world can once again hunt down dracula during their next board game night.

Fury of Dracula Board Game (5th Edition)

For those familiar with either the Fantasy Flight Games’ 3rd or WizKids’ 4th editions, the 5th edition is largely the same but for everyone else, Fury of Dracula is a one-versus-many with one person playing as the count and up to four other players controlling the hunters. As I mentioned a moment ago, this is a hidden movement game, where Dracula will be moving around the map, placing cards face down noting where he is and was, leaving dangers in his wake, while the hunters try to trap and kill the vampire lord. Each round, consisting of a Day and Night phase, begins with the hunters moving, supplying themselves with tools and special event cards, purchasing travel tickets, or searching for their target. During the day, these actions are generally safer, while attempting to resupply invites potentially hazardous events that may help Dracula instead.

Fury of Dracula Board Game (5th Edition) Images

Dracula’s turn is a bit less eventful, but debatably more important. Once all the hunters have taken their nighttime actions, Dracula is then able to move to a new location, placing face down a new location card on their growing trail and an encounter card. These encounters, secret much like the locations themselves until a hunter uncovers them, may spawn enemies, create diversions and delays for the hunters, or worse. Should one of these ever move off the board, “maturing” as it’s referred to, the despair track will increase, putting Dracula that much closer to securing his victory!

Unlike other hidden movement games, such as Whitehall Mystery (another personal favorite of mine) that is purely a game of cat and mouse, Fury of Dracula incorporates a combat mechanism. During situations where the hunters have cornered Dracula, both sides pick a card from their hands, composed of moves or helpful items like holy bullets and pistols on the side of the hunters, and then flip them, then resolve their effects. Despite the rather simplistic nature of these fights, it also has led to some of the tensest moments in board games I’ve ever had. Moments when misreading my opponent led them to safety, or one especially board-flipping time when I expected Dracula, who being only one hit away from death, to flee, only to have him decide to bite and knock me out instead. A defeat that pushed the despair track past its end, and handing the win to Dracula. Utterly infuriating, but also one of the aspects of Fury of Dracula that sets it above many other hidden movement games for me.

In addition to redone artwork (more on that in a bit), this new fifth edition does offer a couple of optional new elements that can shake up the formula a bit for those Fury vets out there. First is the addition of a fifth hunter to pick from, Jonathan Harker, who previously had been relegated to just an ally card. Mr. Harker now can be picked to replace one of the other hunters, and has some powerful abilities that should certainly help the good guys out. He’s able to not only deal additional damage when hitting Dracula but also, similar to his wife Mina, can force him to announce if Jonathan is in an adjacent spot. While a neat addition, it also feels like a bit of a halfbaked attempt too. Unlike the other hunters, Mr. Harker doesn’t get his own unique event card, and instead can simply use the one made for the hunter that he replaces. The balance of the game also doesn’t quite feel like it’s been balanced for him, and I found that when both Harkers were on the board, with their tracking talents, it made for a decently harder time for Dracula. He’s a fun “sometimes” change, but I plan to stick with my normal squad for most games.

Fury of Dracula is typically a game that can take a surprising amount of time, with some games I’ve played lasting past the four hour mark, and the second new addition with 5th edition is a faster game mode that can cut that in half or more. This new faster variant removes a couple of cards and blocks off a couple of the regions of the map (damn that Black Plague) while setting the board state roughly around where it would be after a “week” (about a third of the way through), granting hunters some items to start, Dracula with some damage, despair up a bit, and a few other tweaks. By-and-large I found this new variant to be a solid choice and makes Fury of Dracula a much more viable option on a weeknight. The smaller region and other adjustments (such as the instantaneous water movement and removing the single value train tickets) can make things far more swinging where getting away and staying hidden as Dracula can be more challenging. Again, just like with Harker, it works, but I’m curious how much balance testing went into it.

As one would expect from a new edition of a game, it isn’t usually just the gameplay or mechanics that get a refresh, but the artwork too, and it’s here where the 5th edition sees its biggest departure. Not because the map changes (though the town of Whitby, which plays an important role in the story of Bram Stoker’s original Dracula novel, is finally included) but the aesthetic has changed. And it’s also here where I think the new edition takes a step backwards from the third and fourth editions.

With exception of Dracula’s location cards, the artwork for the event, encounter, item, and combat cards all have ditched the dramatic and detailed full color artwork of the earlier iterations in favor of what I would describe as drawings you may see in an old Victorian-era newspaper. These black-and-white illustrations work, but just don’t have the same impact, with some appearing, dare I say, even a bit corny? The “Dark Call” card for example, now features Dracula staring at the moon with a few bats in front of him, compared to earlier versions where he appears to be basking in the night with hordes of bats all around, against a stormy sky. Then there is the new “Misdirect” which basically makes him look like Batman from The Animated Series, as opposed to a mysterious man in a top hat, lurking in the fog. Hunter and Dracula character cards don’t fare much better either, with the portraits replaced with sepia-tinted photographs of the character. Which, now that I think about it, could you even take a picture of Dracula? I mean, vampires don’t have reflections in mirrors, so can you photograph them? Oh well, questions for another time.

articles.title: Halloween: The Game Review So Far
articles.summary: So far this asymmetrical horror game is more trick than treat.
articles.body:
Plenty of things are terrifying about a man in a boiler suit creeping up behind you, but it's hard to be scared of Halloween: The Game's Michael Myers when he strolls around the neighborhood with all the urgency of a retiree on a golf course. Admittedly, my early experience with the latest asymmetrical survival horror based on a famous movie came without the obligatory day one patch, so everything I’ve seen so far comes with that giant, flashing caveat. But after several hours, my immediate reaction is that this just isn't ready. I would barely think it’s ready if it were labeled asan early access game, which it’s not. Clumsy, buggy, and often frustrating, Halloween: The Game seems in need of considerable polish and bug squishing.

Developer Illfonic is, of course, almost synonymous with asymmetrical horror at this point, if not quite able to break the stranglehold Behaviour Interactive has with Dead by Daylight. In keeping with the traditions of the genre, you either play on your own as the killer, Michael Myers, and rampage through the town, or you work with up to three other humans and a handful of AI companions to loot items and keep yourself alive long enough to find, open, and escape the streets of Haddonfield on Halloween night in 1978.

Halloween: The Game Gameplay Screenshots

Because of Illfonic's back catalog, I came in with high expectations, and knowing Halloween creator John Carpenter was also involved sent them soaring even further. You'd think, with the best part of a decade's learning and all that asym trial and error behind it, Halloween: The Game would be the most polished of all Illfonic's games. But — so far at least — that just doesn't seem to be the case.

Animations are broken or missing completely. I've had hard crashes that sent me back to my PS5 dash, averaging at least one an hour. Combat is beyond janky — several times now, I've stabbed a player and had my weapon phase right through them. Often the sound gets messed up, so when I open a door to my left , I hear it to my right , which is hugely irritating given sound is vital to a stealth horror game. And on two occasions, a quick time event bugged out and trapped me in a broken animation, giving Myers all the time in the world to step up right behind me. That was just as much fun and not-at-all-frustrating as it sounds.

The NPC AI is also hysterically stupid. Once, playing as Myers, I (loudly) busted through a front door and found all three remaining NPCs in the same room, still standing at the same window. I had executed two before the remaining one decided it was time to make a run for it.

It's galling because there are some excellent ideas here. I had a great time with The Texas Chain Saw Massacre 's spin on asymmetrical horror back in 2023, but within days it was clear no one wanted to play as Leatherface because it was so much easier — and considerably more fun — to clock up XP and escape as a survivor.

In Halloween: The Game, however, Illfonic seems to have really worked to balance the odds between killer and civilian, and Myers is a blast to play. Even though he never, ever runs, making it next to impossible to take out a player if they've seen you, his special abilities — snuffing out all the lights in the immediate area; jumping from shadow to shadow; detecting nearby players — help mitigate that deeply unsatisfactory walking speed, especially if you nail the timing. Plus, the execution mechanic is a neat shortcut if you manage to get close enough to… well, execute it. The death animations, if often out of sync, are brilliantly brutal, too, particularly if you manage to catch a civilian, by a window or next to an electric oven. (I'm sure there's more still to discover!)

Best of all, this isn't just four humans against one killer. As Myers, your job is to wipe the map clean of all survivors, human and NPC alike. As a civilian, you need to creep around the deliciously 70s-inspired maps — everything, from the cars to the decor to the rotary phones, is on point here, not to mention the fashion! — quietly warning NPCs and instructing them to either hide, follow you, or escape.

There are plenty of items to gather as you creep through residential homes, including offensive weapons, defensive tools, and a host of goodies to bolster the odds of getting out of there unscathed. You'll never be able to take Myers out completely — just like the movies, this is a dude who does not know how to take the hint and die — but you can temporarily immobilize him with the right timing and the right equipment.

That said, why do we have to sit and watch Myers finish killing off idiot NPCs if all the human players are already dead? You're given QTEs when spectating — I hate them; there are too many, they're too boring, and I swear there's occasionally an input delay — but it's so tedious, especially as the maps are pretty chunky and make hunting down one last survivor time-consuming.

Vikki Blake's Most Terrifying Horror Games Ever List

And it just doesn't perform well. Even beyond the poor AI and broken QTEs, I experienced numerous crashes, rubberbanding, and framerate drops for no discernible reason. Characters sometimes walked three feet off the ground. Interacting with items is completely hit-or-miss — half the time you can pick stuff up or remove a chain with a bolt cutter; half the time you cannot. Oh, and sometimes you can open a door, step through it, lock it, and then find yourself back outside the front, unable to get back in.

Like I said, I need to play on the launch patch before finalizing my thoughts — but, generally speaking, a day one update is rarely a miracle fix for all of a review build’s issues. Still, I'll be back once I've spent some time on the live servers with both the single and multiplayer modes (so far the former has completely underwhelmed me — again, mostly due to idiotic NPCs). I'd also like to better understand how the card perk system works and experiment with all the civilians' passive abilities. For now, though, it's difficult to recommend Halloween: The Game to anyone other than a horror fan with a Michael Myers shrine in their home (now that's a scary thought) or those with deep, deep affection for asymmetrical games.

articles.title: Wonder Woman Casting Rumors Heat Up as Fans Suspect James Gunn Secretly Picked Adria Arjona for the Role
articles.summary: DC fans are convinced the DCU's Wonder Woman will be played by Adria Arjona after she posted a video of her workout routine ahead of Man of Tomorrow.
articles.body:
DC fans are convinced the DCU's Wonder Woman will be played by Adria Arjona after she posted a video of her workout routine ahead of Man of Tomorrow .

As the DCU navigates its ups and downs , all eyes are on DC Studios co-CEO and director James Gunn to deliver next year's Superman sequel. Arjona is just one part of the equation that will help bring David Corenswet's Last Son of Krypton back to the big screen, but fans think she knows more than she's letting on when it comes to the part she'll play in the wider DCU.

Mixed in with a variety of other superhero parts – including Milly Alcock's Supergirl , Aaron Pierre's John Stewart , and Xolo Maridueña as Blue Beetle – Arjona was previously said to be playing the role of DC deep cut Maxima . She reportedly landed the part in April of this year, but fans think Gunn and company are misleading fans in hopes of a big Sadie Sink/Spider-Man-style surprise with Man of Tomorrow.

Rumors that her role would eventually be revealed as Wonder Woman surfaced shortly after her casting, but nothing has stoked the flames quite like a video posted by Women's Health yesterday . The seven-minute highlight showed Arjona's "intense boxing and strength workout," letting viewers peek into how she trains for the parts she plays. Although she explicitly mentioned that training helped her prepare to play Celeste in Onslaught, a later segment brings her rumored DC career into focus.

"I've never felt strong, but it's hard," Arjona said as headlines related to Wonder Woman rumors flased on the screen. "Well, I think the excitement of playing the woman I'm playing gives me everything I need to wake up. Physically, it's exhausting, but it's all for the better good. The better good? Is that English? The greater good!"

The emphasis, of course, is on "the woman I'm playing." The footage of her intense workout routine coupled with that one specific line has turned everyday rumors into a full-blown whirlwind of speculation, and fans aren't letting up.

She's soo playing Wonder woman pic.twitter.com/uR945bnntP — ~ (@toiinfinite) September 4, 2026

“The woman I’m playing” …Holy shit you are playing Wonder Woman pic.twitter.com/q8uP3Banml — Alex From Florida ☽☾ (@floridian_alex) September 4, 2026

“The woman I’m playing” …Holy shit you are playing Wonder Woman pic.twitter.com/q8uP3Banml

Adria Arjona's response to a fan calling her Wonder Woman at the 'Onslaught' Q&A "Thank you guys so much for coming" pic.twitter.com/oHky4LZDPx — Superman Saga News (@SuperSagaNews) September 4, 2026

Adria Arjona's response to a fan calling her Wonder Woman at the 'Onslaught' Q&A "Thank you guys so much for coming" pic.twitter.com/oHky4LZDPx

"Really makes you wonder what woman she's playing," one fan said .

"Like come on man," another added . "This is Wonder Woman."

"Again, we all know she is Wonder Woman but it would be so hilarious if she was doing all this for Maxima," another person joked .

The internet thinks Arjona at least already looks like she could feasibly weild the Lasso of Truth as Diana Prince, but she's not been confirmed to play Wonder Woman just yet. However, it's that very mystery that has fans all riled up – but some of Gunn's comments aren't helping, either.

In July 2025, nearly one year before Arjona joined the Man of Tomorrow cast, fans caught wind that the DC director had started following the actress on Instagram . What was written off as a reach then has now been reassessed, and Gunn's comments at the time might be very telling when it comes to the future of the DCU.

Honestly that’s a good way to tell if you made a great casting decision when you announce Adria Arjona is in the film and everyone immediately clocks that it’s for Wonder Woman lol — MaceAhWindu (@MaceAhWindu) September 4, 2026

Honestly that’s a good way to tell if you made a great casting decision when you announce Adria Arjona is in the film and everyone immediately clocks that it’s for Wonder Woman lol

DC really cooked with this Wonder Woman casting…. Simply no notes 10/10 pic.twitter.com/3fNM8bcZPp — Jin x Supreme ❤️‍🔥 (@Jinsakuu) September 3, 2026

DC really cooked with this Wonder Woman casting…. Simply no notes 10/10 pic.twitter.com/3fNM8bcZPp

"I followed Adria Arjona on Instagram, but everybody came out, 'He just followed her, that means she’s Wonder Woman! That means she’s Wonder Woman!'" he said.

"She’d be a great Wonder Woman, by the way. But she was in a movie that I made seven years ago. We’ve been friends and have known each other since that time. I followed her then, I didn’t just follow her. People just notice these things all the time."

So, Arjona is keeping her role in the Superman sequel a secret, fans think she looks like a great Wonder Woman, and even Gunn admitted she'd be great for the role. If DC Studios has indeed cast her for one of the biggest members of the Justice League, then it might want to play its cards a little closer to its chest.

No matter what internet sleuths uncover, though, it doesn't change the fact that Gunn and the DCU have not currently named their Wonder Woman. Hopefully, we won't have to wait much longer to find out more, though.

HBO Max show Lanterns has revealed more about the comic book universe with each episode, with more set to peel back even more layers in the weeks ahead.
